authority: CLAUDE.md §12.1 to §12.4 (reviewability, the four status categories, a missing input is a failure not a fabrication) and §15 (explicit failure over fabricated completion).

§9.1 and §9.4: the preserved run record under docs/ is the durable form of a run manifest that lives in gitignored runtime state, and this report with its decision record is the durable form of what was found.
§9.6: the schema registry reflects the repository, so the preserved record schema is registered.
§17.1: the check sits in the CLI entry point; the DAG scheduler, the agent runtime and the gate evaluator are untouched. §17.6.2 and §17.6.3: nothing here evaluates a gate or writes a gate result.
Subticket A of the ticket 'Change scenarios and shadow comparison' in plans/dev_graph_demo_tickets.md supplies the three acceptance boxes.
question_asked: Does a run id that is not a plain identifier fail at the entry point with the rule named; does the comparison read the preserved manifest by slug and report the true run id; and do the eight advisories compared against the Phase 8 run return a diagnostic or a refusal whose kind is not malformed_request?
answer: Three of three met. The entry point refuses the id with exit code 3 and the rule in the message, and no run directory is created. The reader reaches the Phase 8 run through docs/tier4_orchestration_state/run_records/import-uuid-print-uuid.uuid4.json, checks that the record names the run asked for, and the comparison records the true id. All eight comparisons against that run return no_reuse_decision: the run is reached and its manifest holds no reuse_decisions key. That is a diagnostic about the run, not about the request, and the box is met as a refusal. A real diagnostic needs a run that recorded a decision, which is subticket D.

acceptance_criteria.1_a_non_plain_run_id_fails_at_the_entry_: MET. tests/runner/test_run_id_rule.py TestTheEntryPoint: exit code 3, 'not a plain identifier' and RUN_ID_RULE in the error, .claude/runs absent afterwards; also in --json mode.
acceptance_criteria.2_the_comparison_reads_the_preserved_man: MET. tests/runner/test_dev_graph_shadow.py TestPreservedRunRecordFallback and TestComparingUnderTheTrueRunId: the mis-pasted id is read by slug, a plain id is never served from a copy, the live directory is never probed with an unsafe id, a record of another schema or naming another run is refused as malformed_record, and the writer produces a comparison carrying the true run id.
acceptance_criteria.3_the_eight_advisories_compared_against_: MET as a refusal. tests/test_demo_change_scenarios.py pins eight comparisons against the true run id, each refused with kind no_reuse_decision and offender the preserved record. The scenario records were regenerated by tools/run_demo_change_scenarios.py and reproduce byte-equal under --check.

what_was_checked_and_how.the_rule: runner.run_context.RUN_ID_RE is the one definition. tests/runner/test_run_id_rule.py pins that the shadow reader's is_plain_run_id is the same object, that every run id the suite already passes to main() satisfies it, that the slug of any string satisfies it, and that the mis-pasted id slugifies to the file name already on disk.
what_was_checked_and_how.the_entry_point: main() is called in-process with the mis-pasted id and with 'bad id', in text and --json modes, against an empty temporary repo root. Exit code, message and the absence of a runs directory are asserted.
what_was_checked_and_how.the_reader: Against the synthetic dev-graph fixture: a plain id is read from the live manifest and never from a preserved copy, even when the live manifest is absent; the mis-pasted id is read by slug; Path.is_file is spied to show .claude/runs is never probed with it; schema and run-id mismatches refuse as malformed_record; an unsafe id with no preserved record refuses as malformed_request naming the record path; a missing key, a null and an empty map all refuse as no_reuse_decision.
what_was_checked_and_how.the_preserve_tool: tests/test_preserve_run_manifests.py seeds runs under a temporary root: the file is named by the shared slug and carries the schema id and both id flags; an absent key is copied as null; a recorded map is copied as is; the note for a Phases 1 to 6 run and for a run that dispatched Phase 8 say different and true things; and the tool's --check mode passes against the live world when .claude/runs is present.
what_was_checked_and_how.the_comparisons: tools/run_demo_change_scenarios.py was rerun. All sixteen comparisons are refused with no_reuse_decision: eight against the Phases 1 to 6 run (live manifest, no key) and eight against the Phase 8 run (preserved record, null). Both tools' --check modes pass.

Confirmed: The entry point refuses a non-plain run id before any run directory exists, with the rule named.
The reader reaches the Phase 8 run through its preserved record and the comparison carries the true run id.
All eight comparisons against the Phase 8 run refuse with no_reuse_decision, offender the preserved record.
The Phase 8 run's manifest holds no reuse_decisions key (read from the manifest, and copied as null).
Both preserved records and all sixteen scenario files reproduce byte-equal under their tools' --check modes.
Inferred: The three drafting nodes of the Phase 8 run produced not_reused decisions that were never persisted: the nodes are released in the manifest, the run was the first to draft, and the scheduler's record_reuse_decision call sits on the reuse branch only (parent record F2).
Unresolved: Whether the comparison classifies a real pair of verdicts correctly on this world: no run here records a decision, so the question stays with subticket D.

findings: F1 — the Phase 8 run holds no reuse decision; naming it yields no_reuse_decision, not a diagnostic (open, subticket D).
F2 — three stray Tier 4 files carry the first word of the mis-pasted id in their names; left as they are, new ones are prevented.
F3 — the preserved copy of the Phase 8 run was stale and its note false for that run; closed by rerunning the tool.
recorded_in: docs/tier4_orchestration_state/dev_graph/change_scenarios/index.json and the seven scenario records beside it
note: No gate was evaluated and no gate result written (§17.1.4, §17.6.2, §17.6.3). No phase was dispatched. No manifest was edited. Nothing in the shadow lane is read at runtime.
